intro.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application that keeps a user's login status synchronized across multiple browser tabs. You will learn how to use the browser's localStorage API and the window 'storage' event to detect and react to changes made in other tabs. The core programming concept involves managing shared state across different instances of your app using event-driven communication. You'll implement this by creating a custom React hook that listens for storage updates and updates the app's authentication state accordingly. This is a practical introduction to handling real-world scenarios where users interact with your app in multiple windows.
intro.usecase: Multi-tab auth sync is essential for modern web applications where users frequently work across multiple browser tabs. For example, banking dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and productivity tools like Google Workspace need to maintain consistent authentication state across all open tabs. When a user logs out in one tab, all other tabs should immediately reflect this change to prevent security vulnerabilities and confusing user experiences. Developers implement this pattern to ensure that sensitive data remains protected and users don't encounter authentication errors when switching between tabs.
